result.topic_en: Properties of the inverse tangent integral Φ(x)=∫_0^x tan⁻¹t/t dt, including its functional equation, power series, and several trigonometric series identities with particular cases.
result.transcription:
Add ms a 94 18 (65) \quad (65) \quad (1)

Let
$\Phi(x) = \int_0^x \frac{\tan^{-1}t}{t}\,dt.$
Then, changing $t$ into $1/t$, it is easy to see that, if $x>0$,
(1) $\Phi(x) - \Phi(\tfrac{1}{x}) = \tfrac12\pi\log x.$
It is also clear that, if $-1 \le x \le 1$, then
(2) $\Phi(x) = \frac{x}{1^2} - \frac{x^3}{3^2} + \frac{x^5}{5^2} - \frac{x^7}{7^2} + \cdots\cdots.$
The following results can easily be proved by differentiating both sides with respect to $x$.
If $0<x<\tfrac12\pi$, then
(3) $\frac{\sin 2x}{1^2} + \frac{\sin 6x}{3^2} + \frac{\sin 10x}{5^2} + \cdots\cdots$
$= \Phi(\tan x) - x\log\tan x.$
As particular cases of (3) we have
(4) $\sqrt2\left(\frac{1}{1^2} - \frac{1}{5^2} + \frac{1}{9^2} - \frac{1}{13^2} + \cdots\right) = \Phi(\sqrt2-1) + \frac{\pi}{8}\log(1+\sqrt2) + \frac{\pi^2}{16};$
(5) $\Phi(1) = \tfrac32\Phi(2-\sqrt3) + \tfrac18\pi\log(2+\sqrt3).$
If $0<x<\tfrac12\pi$, then
(6) $\frac{\cos x+\sin x}{1^2} + \frac12\cdot\frac{\cos^3x+\sin^3x}{3^2} + \frac{1.3}{2.4}\cdot\frac{\cos^5x+\sin^5x}{5^2} + \cdots$
$= \Phi(\tan x) + \tfrac12\pi\log(2\cos x);$
and
(7) $\frac{\sin x}{1^2}\cos x + \frac{\sin 2x}{2^2}\cos^2x + \frac{\sin 3x}{3^2}\cos^3x + \cdots$
$= \Phi(\tan x) + \tfrac12\pi\log\cos x - x\log\sin x.$
